stem: Liquids that conduct electricity are called __________.
solution: Liquids that allow electric current to pass are conductors; those that conduct due to ions are electrolytes.

stem: Liquids that do not conduct electricity are called __________.
solution: Insulating liquids, like distilled water and oil, do not conduct electricity.

stem: Most liquids that conduct electricity are solutions of __________.
solution: Solutions of acids, bases and salts conduct electricity because they contain ions.

stem: Distilled (pure) water is a __________ of electricity.
solution: Pure distilled water has no dissolved ions, so it is a poor conductor of electricity.

stem: Adding common salt to distilled water makes it __________.
solution: Dissolved salt provides ions, turning distilled water into a good conductor.

stem: Ordinary tap water conducts electricity because it contains __________.
solution: Tap water contains dissolved salts and minerals that provide ions, so it conducts electricity.

stem: When electric current passes through a conducting liquid, it can cause a __________ effect.
solution: The passage of current through a conducting solution causes chemical changes — the chemical effect of current.

stem: The chemical effect of electric current can be seen as __________.
options: gas bubbles, deposits of metal, or colour changes at the electrodes
solution: Chemical effects include gas formation, metal deposits, and colour changes at the electrodes.

stem: The process of depositing a layer of one metal over another using electricity is called __________.
solution: Electroplating deposits a metal layer on an object using electric current through a solution.

stem: Electroplating is used to coat cheaper metals with a layer of __________.
options: a more attractive or corrosion-resistant metal (like gold, silver or chromium)
solution: Electroplating coats objects with metals like gold, silver or chromium to improve appearance or prevent corrosion.

stem: Chromium plating is done on car parts and taps mainly because chromium __________.
options: resists corrosion and gives a shiny appearance
solution: Chromium is hard, shiny and corrosion-resistant, so it is electroplated onto car parts, taps and cycle handlebars.

stem: Iron objects are coated with zinc by galvanisation to __________.
solution: Galvanising (zinc coating) protects iron from rusting.

stem: Tin is electroplated on iron cans used for storing food because tin is __________.
options: less reactive and does not react with food
solution: Tin is less reactive and safe, so tin-plated iron cans are used to store food without contamination.

stem: In electroplating, the object to be plated is connected to the __________ terminal of the battery.
solution: The object to be plated is made the cathode (connected to the negative terminal), where the metal deposits.

stem: When electricity is passed through acidulated water, it breaks up into __________.
solution: Passing current through acidified water splits it into hydrogen and oxygen — a chemical effect.

stem: In the electrolysis of water, hydrogen gas collects at the __________.
solution: Hydrogen (twice the volume of oxygen) collects at the cathode (negative electrode).

stem: A simple tester using an LED can show that a liquid conducts electricity because the LED __________.
solution: If the liquid conducts, the circuit is complete and the LED glows, indicating conduction.

stem: An LED is often used instead of a bulb to test weak conduction because it __________.
options: glows even when a very small current passes
solution: An LED lights up even with a very small current, making it good for detecting weak conduction.

stem: The passage of electric current through a conducting solution deposits metal on an electrode; this shows the __________ effect of current.
solution: Depositing metal at an electrode during electrolysis is a chemical effect of electric current.

stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity in the liquid state?
solution: Lemon juice (an acid) contains ions and conducts electricity; oil, distilled water and honey are poor conductors.

stem: The electrodes used in electrolysis are usually made of __________.
options: conducting materials like metals or carbon
solution: Electrodes are conductors (metals or carbon rods) that carry current into and out of the solution.

stem: The two electrodes in an electrolytic cell are called the __________.
solution: The positive electrode is the anode and the negative electrode is the cathode.

stem: Which of the following would light the bulb in a conduction test?
solution: Salt solution conducts electricity (has ions) and lights the bulb; sugar solution, kerosene and distilled water do not.

stem: In electroplating silver on a spoon, the source of silver is usually the __________.
solution: The silver anode dissolves into the solution and silver deposits onto the spoon (cathode).

stem: Which of the following statements about pure water is TRUE?
options: It is a poor conductor because it lacks ions
It is a very good conductor
solution: Pure (distilled) water has no dissolved ions, so it conducts electricity poorly.

stem: We should not touch electrical switches or appliances with wet hands because __________.
options: water on the skin conducts electricity and can cause a shock
solution: Water (with dissolved salts on skin) conducts electricity, so wet hands increase the risk of a shock.

stem: Electroplating jewellery with gold makes cheaper metal ornaments __________.
options: look like gold and resist tarnishing
solution: Gold electroplating gives cheaper ornaments a gold appearance and protects them from tarnishing.

stem: The chemical effect of current is used in the extraction of metals like __________ from their compounds.
solution: Reactive metals like aluminium are extracted by electrolysis, using the chemical effect of current.

stem: When current passes through copper sulphate solution with copper electrodes, copper is deposited on the __________.
solution: During electrolysis of copper sulphate with copper electrodes, copper deposits on the cathode.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a good conductor of electricity in solution?
solution: Sugar solution has no ions and does not conduct; salt solution, dilute acid and lemon juice conduct.

stem: The gas that collects in double the amount during electrolysis of water is __________.
solution: Water splits into hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 volume ratio, so twice as much hydrogen is produced.

stem: In electroplating, the metal that gets deposited comes from __________.
options: the metal salt solution and the metal anode
solution: The metal ions in the salt solution (replenished by the dissolving anode) are deposited on the object.

stem: Fruits and vegetables can act as weak conductors because their juices contain __________.
solution: Juices of fruits and vegetables contain acids and salts that provide ions, so they conduct weakly.

stem: The chemical effect of electric current does NOT occur in __________.
options: a dry piece of metal wire
solution: A dry metal wire carries current without a chemical change; chemical effects occur in conducting solutions.

stem: Which of the following is an application of the chemical effect of current?
solution: Electroplating and electrolysis use the chemical effect; heaters/bulbs use heating, bells use magnetic effects.

stem: To make bath taps shiny and corrosion-free, they are electroplated with __________.
solution: Bath taps are chromium-plated for shine and corrosion resistance.

stem: Which of the following will show that a liquid is a conductor?
options: The bulb/LED in the circuit glows
solution: If the liquid conducts, the circuit completes and the bulb or LED glows.

stem: The formation of bubbles at the electrodes when current passes through a solution shows __________.
options: gases are being released (a chemical effect)
solution: Bubbles indicate gases being liberated at the electrodes, a chemical effect of the current.

stem: The purpose of coating an iron object with a less reactive metal by electroplating is to __________.
solution: A protective coating of a less reactive metal prevents the iron from corroding/rusting.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a metal with its electroplating use?
options: Chromium – on car parts for shine and protection
solution: Chromium is electroplated on car parts and taps for shine and corrosion resistance.

stem: The safe reason to use distilled water in car batteries (rather than tap water) is that distilled water __________.
options: lacks impurities that could interfere with the battery
solution: Distilled water lacks dissolved impurities, so it does not interfere with the chemistry of the battery.

stem: Which observation would confirm that a solution conducts electricity in a tester circuit?
options: The LED glows and bubbles may appear at the electrodes
solution: A glowing LED (and gas bubbles at electrodes) confirms the solution conducts electricity.

stem: Electroplating helps save costly metals because __________.
options: only a thin layer of the costly metal is needed over a cheaper base
the whole object is made of the costly metal
solution: A thin electroplated layer of a costly metal over a cheap base gives the desired properties at lower cost.

stem: Which of the following pairs a liquid with its correct conducting nature?
solution: Dilute sulphuric acid conducts electricity; oil, distilled water and sugar solution are poor conductors.

stem: Which safety rule relates to the chemical effect of electricity in the home?
options: Keep electrical appliances dry and do not handle them with wet hands
solution: Because water conducts electricity, keeping appliances dry and not using them with wet hands prevents shocks.

stem: When a solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed, its blue colour fades over time because __________.
options: copper is deposited out of the solution
solution: As copper deposits at the cathode, copper leaves the solution, so its blue colour gradually fades (unless replenished by a copper anode).

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about conductors and insulators of electricity in liquids?
options: Solutions of acids, bases and salts conduct; pure water and oils do not
solution: Acid, base and salt solutions conduct due to ions; pure water and oils are poor conductors.

stem: The main idea behind electroplating is to use the __________ of electric current.
solution: Electroplating relies on the chemical effect of electric current to deposit a metal layer.

stem: In electroplating, the object to be coated is made the __________.
solution: The object to be plated is the cathode, where the metal from the solution deposits.

stem: Which of the following conducts electricity because it contains ions?
solution: Salt solution has dissolved ions and conducts electricity; the others are poor conductors.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Chemical Effects of Electric Current' is that:
options: electric current passing through conducting liquids causes chemical effects, used in electrolysis and electroplating
solution: The chapter shows that current through conducting solutions produces chemical effects (gas, deposits, colour change), applied in electrolysis and electroplating.

stem: When electric current passes through a conducting solution, it produces a __________ effect.
solution: Current through a conducting solution produces a chemical effect.

stem: The chemical effect of current can cause __________ of gas at the electrodes.
solution: Gas bubbles may form at electrodes due to the chemical effect of current.

stem: Most liquids that conduct electricity are solutions of acids, bases or __________.
solution: Solutions of acids, bases and salts conduct electricity.

stem: Distilled water is a __________ conductor of electricity.
solution: Distilled water has no dissolved ions, so it conducts electricity poorly.

stem: Adding common salt to distilled water makes it a __________ conductor.
solution: Dissolved salt provides ions, making the water a good conductor.

stem: The process of depositing a layer of a metal on another using electricity is called __________.
solution: Electroplating uses the chemical effect of current to coat an object with a metal.

stem: Electroplating is done to protect metals from __________ and to improve appearance.
solution: Electroplating protects metals from corrosion and gives an attractive finish.

stem: Chromium is electroplated on objects like taps because it __________.
solution: Chromium plating gives a shiny, hard, corrosion-resistant surface.

stem: A simple tester used to check if a liquid conducts electricity uses a cell, wires and a __________.
solution: A tester uses a bulb or LED that glows if the liquid conducts electricity.

stem: An LED is used instead of a bulb in a tester because it glows even with a __________ current.
solution: An LED can glow even with a weak current that would not light a bulb.

stem: When current passes through acidified water, the gases released at the electrodes are hydrogen and __________.
solution: Electrolysis of acidified water gives hydrogen and oxygen.

stem: In electroplating, the object to be plated is connected to the __________ terminal.
solution: The object to be coated is made the cathode (negative terminal).

stem: Rubber and plastic are examples of materials that __________ conduct electricity.
solution: Rubber and plastic are insulators and do not conduct electricity.

stem: Even weakly conducting liquids can be detected using a __________ tester.
solution: A magnetic needle deflects near a wire carrying even a weak current, detecting conduction.

stem: The passage of electricity through a conducting liquid causes __________ changes in the liquid.
solution: The chemical effect of current causes chemical changes in a conducting liquid.

stem: Lemon juice and vinegar are __________ of electricity.
solution: Lemon juice and vinegar are acidic solutions that conduct electricity.

stem: Most metals are good conductors, while most non-metals are __________.
solution: Most non-metals are poor conductors (insulators) of electricity.

stem: The deposition of copper on an electrode from copper sulphate solution is an example of the __________ effect of current.
solution: Copper depositing from its solution is due to the chemical effect of current.

stem: Impure water, such as tap water, conducts electricity because it contains dissolved __________.
solution: Tap water contains dissolved salts and minerals that provide ions to conduct current.

stem: Which of the following conducts electricity best?
solution: Salt solution has many ions, so it conducts electricity best among these.

stem: Electroplating helps save costly metals because only a __________ layer is used.
solution: Electroplating uses only a thin layer of the costly metal, saving material.

stem: The main safety precaution when working with electricity and water is to __________.
options: keep them apart and use dry hands
solution: Water conducts electricity and increases shock risk, so keep them apart and use dry hands.
